§ 2Content

§ 3SEGMENTATION

  • Segmentation is the division of an animal's body into repeating, similar units called segments.
  • Segmentation provides redundancy, flexibility, and allows for more efficient locomotion.

Phyla with Segmentation

PhylumType of segmentation
AnnelidaMetameric segmentation — body divided into many similar segments (e.g. earthworm).
ArthropodaBody divided into distinct head, thorax, abdomen (tagmosis).
ChordataInternal segmentation — vertebrae and ribs (vertebral column).

Note

  • In Annelida, segmentation is external and metameric (each segment is a similar repeat).
  • In Arthropoda, segmentation is regionalised (head/thorax/abdomen), with jointed appendages.
  • In Chordata, segmentation is internal — the vertebral column is a series of repeating bones.

§ 4Key concepts

  • Segmentation: division of body into repeating units
  • Annelida: metameric (full)
  • Arthropoda: tagmosis (head + thorax + abdomen)
  • Chordata: internal (vertebrae + ribs)
